Hi Ethan / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate you walking us through the search reranking flow and the peak load pattern. I wanted to capture the technical constraints and the immediate next steps so we can bring the right infra/engineering folks into the follow-up workshop. Key takeaways from today: 

- Primary pain: production reranking is currently CPU-bound and inconsistent under bursty traffic (spikes tied to index refresh and marketing campaigns).
- Goal: deliver a 99th-percentile rerank latency under 120ms for 1k-2k QPS bursts (steady-state baseline ~200 QPS), with seamless failover to lower-cost variants during heavy tail events.
- Model expectations: multi-turn context up to 4k tokens, deterministic ranking output, 8 tokens of answer expected on average, occasional long-form generation for content previews (~512 tokens).
- Data sensitivity: logs must be retained for 90 days; payloads contain PII fields in query text — customer prefers VPC/private deployment.

Technical items I noted for Karthik and the infra team to validate: 
- Target SLOs to validate: p50 ~30-50ms, p95 <120ms for reranking requests at 200 QPS; graceful degradation policy for 1k+ QPS bursts.
- Cold-start behavior expectations: <250ms added for warm-start, acceptable to have sticky routing to pinned instances for active models.
- Model variants: primary (70B quantized) + fallback (13B quantized) — we discussed tradeoffs on quality vs cost; need guidance on when to trigger fallback.

Attachments: I attached the SLO table we sketched and a draft topology for our recommended Dedicated/Private hybrid.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Karthik to provide a short topology + resource estimate and call out KV-cache and batching suggestions (by EOD Tue 3/5).
2) Schedule a 90-minute technical workshop with Atheneum infra + your ML infra (propose Wed 3/7 or Thu 3/8) — include procurement for pricing/contract constraints.
3) Procurement questions (Priya) — we can loop in Monica to align on billing and procurement timeline.

Ethan / Priya — please confirm availability for the workshop and add any missing constraints.

Thanks,

Hannah — thanks for the clear summary. That matches what we want to achieve. A couple of clarifications before the workshop: 

- The 1k-2k QPS bursts are 10-15 minute windows, happening roughly twice per week. We need queuing and graceful degradation, not hard failures.
- For cold-start: we can accept up to 300ms added latency on cold instances but prefer sticky sessions for active queries.
- Security: we require SOC2 evidence and an option for on-prem (air-gapped) later in the year.

We'd like Karthik to call out any implications for model quantization on ranking determinism — we can't have large ranking regressions. Also please include an estimate for peak concurrent memory (KV cache sizing) for a 4k context.

Ethan / Priya — adding the technical summary and an initial topology recommendation below. I'm keeping it high level to align on constraints; we can surface a workshop slide with numbers and a cost delta later.

Short technical readout (answers to your asks):
- Target SLO mapping (rerank endpoint): p50 goal 40ms, p95 goal 120ms for 200 QPS steady-state. For burst windows (~1k QPS), aim for best-effort p95 under 250ms with fallback to smaller variant when sustained >600 QPS.
- Cold-start: recommend warm pools (pre-warmed replicas) and sticky routing. Expect ~150-300ms cold-start overhead per replica depending on model quantization.
- Model & quantization: recommend primary path using a quantized 70B (nf4/int8 depending on kernel availability) for quality. Fallback to a 13B int8 variant when latency or load thresholds are met. We will run a small regression test against your ranking set to measure delta; if regression >1.5% MAE on rank order we adjust thresholds.
- KV-cache sizing: for 4k context with typical tokenization, reserve ~22GB per replica for KV (approx). If you use prefix caching for active sessions, storage per replica increases — we should size for 32GB to be safe if long conversations are common.
- Batching & concurrency: continuous batching improves throughput but raises tail latency. For strict p95 latency targets we suggest small batching windows (3-5ms) and dynamic batch sizing tied to traffic.
- Hardware topology options (initial):
  Option A (Dedicated - single-node): 1x H100 80GB with model sharding + 4 pre-warmed replicas. Best tail latency, higher cost per token. Good for low multitenancy and strict p95.
  Option B (Dedicated - multi-node sharded): 2x H100 80GB (tensor parallel) with throughput headroom. Better for high sustained throughput; slightly higher network overhead.
  Option C (Private hybrid): Front-door hosted routing to Dedicated pool + Private VPC-only workers for sensitive queries. This meets your data retention / VPC requirement while keeping spikes on hosted pool.

Fallback policy suggestion: route by policy — if queue length > X or observed p95 > 140ms for two consecutive 1-min windows, route new requests to 13B fallback cluster or apply soft-sampling (reduce deterministic beam width). We'll define thresholds in the workshop.

Attachments: I uploaded a quick topology sketch and resource estimate: redwood-topology-draft.pdf. I also put a small spreadsheet with estimated memory/CPU/GPU counts into the shared drive.

Open questions for the workshop:
- Atheneum's acceptable rank regression threshold for switching to fallback.
- Procurement lead times for Dedicated capacity (typical lead 2-4 weeks).
- Any additional compliance evidence required beyond SOC2 (e.g., FedRAMP / ISO 27001).

I'll prepare a 6-slide technical briefing and a short runbook mapping failure modes to automatic fallback actions before the workshop.

— Karthik
